lane: Lane G80 — MACS-EDTI (Multi-Scale Anisotropic Cross-Physics Structural & Hydrothermal Conduit Tensor + Topo-Deconfounded Dual-Expert LOQO Ensemble + Expected-DTI Emitter)
hypothesis: Uncatalogued geothermal and Basin-and-Range faults missed by aerial-scarp mapping can be recovered without regional memorization or topographic range-cliff bias by fusing (1) multi-scale 8-azimuth steerable Radon line-integrals (0.9 km, 2.1 km, 3.5 km) across both 1 m 3DEP LiDAR scarplets and subsurface gravity/magnetic basement gradients, (2) +-600 m cross-strike block-throw asymmetry and down-dip hanging-wall MT conductivity/gravity coupling, and (3) DOE GDR-1391 solute geothermometry + USGS/INGENIOUS convective heat-flow + GeoDAWN K/Th potassic alteration plumes inside a strictly out-of-quadrant dual-expert ensemble pairing a slope-propensity-balanced full-physics expert with a 100% topographically-blind pure-subsurface expert, emitted outside the 350 m dead collar.
mechanism: 61 strictly label-free channels (42 pure-subsurface potential-field/strain/seismic/MT/radiometric/geothermometry channels + 19 surface/LiDAR/cross-strike coupling channels) fit strictly Leave-One-Quadrant-Out (fixing IR-80-01 negative-pool truth leakage and IR-80-02 in-quadrant memorization found in GEMSDOE77 H85), fused in de-seamed Bayesian log-odds space (0.34*MACS61 + 0.42*MACS60_MapFree + 0.24*Subsurface41_TopoBlind), and discretely allocated on d(existing_faults) > 3.2 px (submod300, min_sep=2.85 px, 31,492 binary dots).
